dispute.claim_text: The blender stopped working after about two weeks. I think it was defective.

evidence.text: Product listing: countertop blender, standard 1-year manufacturer warranty.
Cardholder to merchant: 'It stopped turning on after two weeks.' No video, photo, or third-party assessment of the fault.
Merchant reply: 'Unit passed QA before shipping. This may be user error; here are troubleshooting steps and warranty contact.'

labels.notes: Hard case. The critical point is a gap: a defective-merchandise claim requires proof of the defect (a photo, video, or third-party assessment), and the cardholder has provided only an unsupported assertion (ev_002). The merchant's generic 'passed QA' (ev_003) is batch-level, not unit-specific, so it does not affirmatively win the point either. Because a defect is potentially provable, the honest output is insufficient - the cardholder should gather proof of the defect and resubmit - rather than accept. Contrast case_010, where the merchant affirmatively proved a matching item (accept).
